newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan electricity workers end five-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Jordan electricity workers end five-day strike.

text.p: More than 2,000 Jordanian private electricity workers ended a five-day strike on Monday after they agreed with the government to set up an arbitration council to resolve their pay dispute, a union official said.

A union official told Reuters that Labour Minister Abdul-Hafez al-Shakhanbeh and union leaders who met late on Sunday with deputies of the Islamic Action Front (IAF) mediators had "agreed to end the strike and return of all workers to their jobs...effective Monday, November 25".

More than 2,000 Electricty Workers Union members had been on strike since Wednesday when the Jordan Electric Power Company rejected demands for bonuses that amount to across-the-board rises of at least 20 percent.
The accord sets up an arbitration council to start its work as of Monday on resolving the pay dispute over bonuses and end of service pay increases.
Workers received a pledge that the company will not fire them for haing gone on strike nor will any legal action be taken against them.
The government had earlier said the strike was illegal and warned it might disband the union if it continued.
Jordanian security forces had prevented workers from staging a sit-in on Sunday after authorising the capital's police to stop the workers from gathering in front of the company headquarters.

Jordan Electric Power Company, a publicly listed company with an over 15 percent holding by state investment bodies, has a concession up to year 2006 to distribute electricity to Amman and the key industrial city of Zarqa.
Average salaries of workers are around 150 dinars.
